summary: A strong, honest Phase 2. Grand/Upright/Electric are genuinely recorded, distinct, offline-bundled CC-BY sample sets (30 real MP3 root notes each, distinct hashes) with complete provenance; Clav/Digital/Misc are honestly declared synthesis. The audio graph is textbook: one AudioContext, per-layer buses, the exact documented ordered chain (Mod1->Mod2->Delay->Amp/EQ->Comp->Reverb), shared Rotary after reverb, master gain -> limiter -> one destination, StrictMode-safe context ownership and clean teardown. All seven effect units are real Web Audio subgraphs with distinct per-type processing, working bypass/dry-wet, an in-loop delay feedback filter, and To Rotary rerouting. 126 real-boundary OfflineAudioContext tests pass (no mocks) and typecheck/lint are clean. The visual surface is faithfully retained from Phase 1. The main gap: String Res is a spec-required performance control that is stored but never bound to audio (effectively decorative), and IMPLEMENTATION_DETAILS mildly overstates that all functional piano controls change audio.

evidence: stage2-desktop.png shows the continuous red chassis, six ordered sections (Performance, Organ, Piano, Program, Synth, Layer Effects), 73-key keybed, and exactly two OLEDs (Program + Synth) — matches reference/nord-stage-4-73.jpg layout and Phase 1 capture with no regression.
regressionPhase2.test.tsx asserts all six section landmarks, 73 keys (43 white + 30 black), two [data-oled] nodes, and every CONTROLS id present under the Phase-2 engine.

Deck is more vertically packed than the real shallow-deck hardware (a retained Phase 1 characteristic); narrow (390x844) retention relies on horizontal scroll inside the chassis container rather than reflow, so right-hand sections require scrolling.
stage2-narrow.png keeps chassis aspect ratio, pins the keybed and honest status strip, and shows no clipped or lost controls.

PianoSection/EffectsSection render coherent LED/selector state: piano type LED list, KB Touch/Dyn Comp/Timbre selectors, per-layer level faders with graphs, effect unit ON LEDs, Delay/Comp/Reverb amber GLOBAL toggles, FX FOCUS + FOCUS A/B/GROUP.

controlBindings.ts drives focus, group, global, per-unit bypass, all-effects bypass, and amp model To Rotary from panel control ids; controlBindings.test.ts verifies reverb-on/group/global/To-Rotary flip the corresponding chain state.
stage2-visual-audit.md documents in-browser that selecting a piano type moves the lit LED and engaging units lights their ON LED with audible change and no console errors.
String Res panel control shows on/off state but does not drive any audio node, so its hardware state is presentation-only despite being a required functional control.

public/samples/{grand,upright,electric} each contain 30 real MPEG layer-III MP3 root notes (A0..C8, minor-third spacing) totaling ~700KB per set; `file` confirms genuine audio and md5 of A4 differs across all three sets — genuinely recorded, not runtime buffers.

IMPLEMENTATION_DETAILS.json declares Grand/Upright/Electric as recorded FluidR3_GM programs (acoustic_grand/honkytonk/electric_piano_1) with CC-BY-3.0 attribution, per-set manifest.json, offline:true, and honestly states a single recorded velocity layer with play-time loudness shaping (not faked multi-velocity).

instruments.test.ts loads all three via injected fetch/decode from the bundled files (status 'ready'), and asserts Grand/Upright/Electric render audibly distinct brightness/RMS fingerprints; Clav/Digital/Misc declared kind 'synth'.
Clav/Digital/Misc are honest synthesis (sampler.ts createSynthVoice recipes) declared under generatedSources, never described as recordings.

audioEngine.ts: each Piano layer (A,B) owns its voices routed only to its own LayerChain bus; noteOn dispatches to enabled layers, per-(layer,pitch) stealing, per-layer polyphony cap, and reap on end.
audioEngine.test.ts proves only enabled layers sound (A only = 1 voice; A+B = 2), per-layer level fader scales that layer's loudness, and octave shift changes rendered pitch.
controlBindings.test.ts: 'layer B enable button' brings B online (1 -> 2 voices) via the piano-on-off-b binding; enable is gated by both piano-on and per-layer toggle.
dispose() and allNotesOff() stop every voice and return activeVoiceCount to 0 (audioEngine.test.ts cleanup test).

pianoControls.test.ts renders real audio proving KB Touch curve (Light>Heavy at soft velocity), Dyn Comp raises soft strokes, velocity monotonic loudness, Timbre changes tone, Unison changes waveform (detuned stack), and Soft Release lengthens the tail.
sampler.ts implements KB Touch exponents, Dyn Comp floor lift, per-family Timbre biquad shaping, Unison detuned voice stacking, and soft/normal release ramps — all bound in controlBindings.ts.

GAP: String Res is a spec-required performance control (piano.json scope.required lists 'KB Touch, Dyn Comp, Timbre, Unison, Soft Release, String Res') but is only stored in PerformanceParams.stringRes and never reaches any audio node — effectively decorative, with no test asserting it changes audio.
IMPLEMENTATION_DETAILS.json states 'all functional Piano controls ... change rendered audio' and lists String Res under functional.piano, mildly overstating coverage for that one control.

Inherited input paths retained: noteRouter/midi/keyboardMap tests plus inputIntegration.test.tsx cover pointer, multitouch, computer keyboard with repeat suppression, MIDI note/velocity/CC64 sustain, and denied MIDI.

instruments.test.ts fallback test: a loader that always throws yields status 'fallback' and still-playable synthesized voices (peak>0.001) without reporting recordings — labeled honest fallback (also surfaced via useAudioEngine + status strip).

audioEngine.test.ts pedals: sustain holds a released note until pedal lift; SUSTPED off means the layer ignores sustain (releases on key up). Soft/sostenuto: soft release is real; no sostenuto claimed.
regressionPhase2.test.tsx exercises rapid pointer play + control toggles with zero console.error and clean unmount (engine 'idle').

audioEngine.ts builds exactly one BaseAudioContext graph: layer buses -> ordered LayerChain -> per-layer level gain -> master GainNode -> DynamicsCompressor limiter -> single ctx.destination; shared RotaryUnit output also feeds master.
audioEngine.test.ts: engine.ctx === the injected context, silence with no notes (peak<0.0001), master level scales rendered loudness, and dispose() cleans up (voice count 0, status idle).

useAudioEngine.ts creates the AudioContext inside the mount effect (never during render) so exactly one context exists per mount (StrictMode-safe), closes it on teardown, and supports an injected OfflineAudioContext for tests.
Short ~20ms linearRamp parameter automation throughout (LayerChain.setLevel, setMasterLevel, effect ramps) for click-free changes.

effects.ts implements Mod1 (tremolo/pan/ring-mod/wah), Mod2 (chorus/flanger/phaser/vibe/ensemble/spin via modulated delay + allpass), Delay (stereo + in-loop feedback biquad), AmpEq (waveshaper drive + 3-band EQ or 24dB filter or To Rotary), Compressor, Reverb (per-type generated convolution IR), Rotary (horn/bass rotor with LFO pan) — all real subgraphs with dry/wet + bypass.

effects.test.ts renders each unit through OfflineAudioContext: Tremolo amplitude variation vs bypass, A-Pan/Rotary stereo width, Delay audible repeats, feedback-filter darkening of late repeats, Amp drive/model distinction, Compressor ratio narrowing, Reverb decay tail growing Booth->Cathedral.
Mod1 types >=4 distinct fingerprints, Mod2 types >=3 distinct; reverb generated IRs declared as generated (not recorded) in IMPLEMENTATION_DETAILS.
Per-type parameters are truly wired (setType rebuilds routing), so labels are not disconnected no-ops.
effects.test.ts 'ordered chain' asserts units() order is exactly Mod1->Mod2->Delay->Amp->Comp->Reverb per layer; Rotary sits after Reverb before master (constructor wiring).
Focus/group/global targeting proven: focus B engages only B's reverb; group engages both; global delay targets both regardless of focus; controlBindings.test.ts mirrors these from panel ids.

all-effects bypass (Layer Effects OFF) neutralizes a Cathedral tail (withFx > bypassed*3); per-unit on/off changes the signal; To Rotary reroutes post-reverb into shared rotary (moving stereo image, routeToRotary flag).
Delay feedback filter sits inside the loop (buildLoop) so repeats are progressively filtered; setDryWet/feedback/tempo are real AudioParam ramps.

controlBindings.ts re-syncs the engine on every ControlStore change (useAudioEngine store.subscribe -> applyAll), so panel selections/parameters immediately change audio and agree with LED/value state.
stage2-visual-audit.md verifies in a real browser that piano-type selection, master level, per-layer enable/level, and effect toggles change audio and match their panel LEDs with zero console errors.
String Res is the one exception where the LED changes but audio does not, a minor feedback-honesty gap.
Status strip reflects real engine status ('Piano ready (recorded + synth voices)', voice count, MIDI denied).
Denied/absent MIDI handled (midi.test.ts + status 'MIDI denied'); no-audio-device path enters labeled silent fallback in useAudioEngine.
Asset-load failure -> status 'fallback' with still-playable synthesis (instruments.test.ts), never reporting recordings it lacks.
regressionPhase2.test.tsx exercises rapid play + piano/effect toggles with no console.error and clean disposal; per-layer polyphony cap steals oldest voice under load.
Master path ends in a DynamicsCompressor limiter (threshold -3, ratio 12) guarding against clipping; no explicit test asserts limiter clamp behavior.

Clean boundaries: sampler.ts (source/voice), audioEngine.ts LayerChain (bus + ordered effects + level), effects.ts (per-unit EffectUnit interface), master gain/limiter, controlBindings.ts (panel->audio), useAudioEngine.ts (one context ownership).
Platform APIs injectable: SampleLoaderDeps (fetchBytes/decode), contextFactory/injectedEngine, so tests run on OfflineAudioContext with no network or devices.
EffectUnit interface and shared makeWetDry mixer give a uniform, Phase-3-extensible unit contract; Rotary is already a shared unit ready for Organ reuse.
Voice abstraction unifies sampled and synth voices (same Voice shape) so the engine treats both uniformly.
126 tests pass across 15 files using node-web-audio-api OfflineAudioContext render() (helpers/audio.ts) — real signals via rms/peak/brightness/stereoWidth/windowRms, explicitly not mocks.

Effect processing, bypass, type distinctness, chain order, focus/group/global routing, To Rotary, delay feedback filtering, reverb decay, compressor ratio, master level, layer ownership, pedals, velocity shaping, and fallback all asserted on rendered audio.
Instrument distinctness and recorded-vs-synth honesty are proven at the boundary (loads real bundled MP3s, asserts distinct spectra).
Structural chain-order test asserts constructor-name order for the documented signal path.
typecheck (tsc --noEmit) and lint (oxlint) both pass clean; consistent naming and per-unit modularity in effects.ts.
Voice reaping (onEnd -> reap) and dispose paths disconnect all nodes; router.panic + engine.dispose + context close on unmount prevent leaks.
Inherited Phase-1 tests preserved (keybed/controls/midi/noteRouter/pianoEngine/App/inputIntegration) and feature-matrix.json maps all Phase 1 + Phase 2 IDs.
Some controlBindings duplication (applyAll vs applyControl repeat the piano/effect param mapping), and String Res carried in PerformanceParams without use is minor dead wiring.

issues: String Res is listed in piano.json scope.required and is carried into PerformanceParams.stringRes and bound in controlBindings, but it never affects any audio node — the control is effectively decorative, and no test asserts it changes audio.

IMPLEMENTATION_DETAILS.json states 'all functional Piano controls ... change rendered audio' and lists String Res under functional.piano, a mild overstatement given String Res produces no audible change.
Narrow (390x844) retention relies on horizontal scroll inside the chassis container rather than reflow, so the right-hand sections (incl. much of Layer Effects) are off-screen until scrolled.
Recorded sets bundle a single velocity layer per root note (honestly declared); acceptable per spec but below true multi-velocity fidelity.
